status_detail: Glynn County adopted data center zoning language, but county communications stated no data center development proposals had been received.
notes: The official county site links to the adopted zoning/subdivision update and meetings. The Current reported Glynn's ordinance permits data centers by special use permit and quoted the county communications director saying there were no proposals; One Hundred Miles also describes Glynn as having an active data center ordinance, not a known project.

project_name: 1401 Hwy. 53 Spur possible data processing center
status_detail: Possible future data center/data processing center site identified; no official project announcement, developer, timeline, or scope released. City of Calhoun later approved a temporary data center moratorium, but reports note Gordon County's county moratorium did not apply inside city limits.
notes: Local reporting says city officials confirmed a roughly 57.27-acre parcel at 1401 Hwy. 53 Spur, zoned IND-G, where a data processing center would be a legal conforming use; the same outlet reported Calhoun's 90-day moratorium on new data center approvals a week later.

status_detail: Operational colocation/data center facility at 2775 Northwoods Pkwy, Norcross; Flexential lists 32,740 sq ft footprint and 1.8 MW critical load UPS capacity.
notes: County official site was checked for local-government coverage; facility-level evidence is from operator and tracker pages. Baxtel lists the site as operational, built 2012, with Atlanta1/Atlanta2 short codes and 20,000 usable sq ft / 1.963 MW across listed components.

status_detail: Planned expansion adjacent to Flexential's existing Norcross facility, with targeted launch in first half of 2028.
notes: Baxtel describes a future facility in planning at/near 2775 Northwoods Parkway NW; Flexential's 2025 real-estate-control announcement confirms the Norcross hub location and expansion strategy, though public capacity for the second building was not found.

status_detail: Operational QTS data center campus with DC1 at 300 Satellite Blvd NW and DC2 at 120 Satellite Blvd NW; QTS says the campus has 100+ MW current planned critical campus capacity.
notes: Operator page provides addresses and campus positioning; QTS Georgia location page states the Suwanee campus is one of its largest-customer campuses and has 100+ MW current planned critical campus capacity. Baxtel lists DC1 operational, built 2000, and DC2 operational, built 2006/acquired by QTS in 2023.

status_detail: Operational enterprise/hyperscale data center at 305 Satellite Blvd, Suwanee; Serverfarm acquired the former AMD facility and later made 110,000 sq ft of capacity available.
notes: Serverfarm's site identifies ATL1 as its Atlanta data center. DCD reported the 153,000 sq ft facility at 305 Satellite Blvd offers 14 MW and originated as AMD's enterprise data center; Baxtel lists it operational and built 2012.

status_detail: CleanSpark acquired the former Sprint/Nextel data center in Norcross on August 6, 2021 for bitcoin mining, adding 20 MW of power with operations expected by late 2021.
notes: Company investor release is the primary evidence: former Sprint/Nextel facility on over 7 acres in Norcross, $6.55M acquisition, 20 MW additional power for mining business. Partnership Gwinnett covered the announcement locally.

aliases: 1900 Level Grove Road mixed-use/data center proposal
status_detail: Proposed 284-acre, $300 million mixed-use development included a portion for a data center; Cornelia City Commission rejected the proposed project/annexation in December 2025.
notes: DCD and WGTJ report the DCA filing for a 284-acre development at 1900 Level Grove Road with a data center component and phased timing from 2028 to 2035. Georgia Trend/Gainesville Times summary says the 284-acre project featuring a possible data center was rejected by Cornelia. Habersham County UDO meeting materials confirm county review of data center regulations.

status_detail: Application for a large data center at 2400 Okelly Road was tabled by Hall County, then withdrawn by the developer at the December 11, 2025 Board of Commissioners meeting.
notes: Hall County agenda items identify Project Turbo, LLC as applicant for special use and rezoning on a 119-acre portion of 2400 Okelly Road for a data center. Planning Commission minutes limited the development to 900,000 sq ft. Later reporting says the proposed $1.2B data center was no longer going forward after the developer withdrew the special-use application.

project_name: Tallapoosa Technology Park / potential data center
aliases: Haralson County Development Authority data center project
developer: Haralson County Development Authority / end user unknown
status_detail: Tallapoosa approved annexation and rezoning of 1,000 additional acres, totaling about 1,600 acres, for industrial development; city announcement says the land could allow a manufacturing plant, distribution warehouse, or data center. Open-records-based local coalition post says an IGA required use solely as a data center and attendant purposes with at least $4.8B capital investment, but no end user has been publicly contracted/confirmed.
notes: Official Tallapoosa PDF confirms May 11, 2026 council approval, annexation/rezoning of 1,000 acres for total 1,600 acres, and possible data center use, while stating no development partners had been contracted. FOX 5 documents public concern over a possible data center. The coalition's GORA-based post is not official but includes claimed IGA details: sale to end user no less than $6.5M, minimum 100 jobs, at least $4.8B capital investment, and at least $500M in site/data center improvements over 10 years.
